proposals.before: Ji Rong of Liaodong cowed the northern tribes until his name carried across the sea; Hui, Mo, Wa, and Korea all sent envoys from immense distances, and from the Zhanghe and Yonghe eras onward diplomatic traffic never stopped.
proposals.after: Ji Rong of Liaodong cowed the northern tribes until his name carried across the sea; Hui, Mo, Wa, and Han all sent envoys from immense distances, and from the reigns of Emperors Zhang and He onward diplomatic traffic never stopped.
proposals.reason: 章、和 names Emperors Zhang and He, not Zhanghe or Yonghe eras; 韓 is Han, not Korea.

proposals.before: At that time the Liaodong governor Ji Rong awed the north with his might; his reputation reached beyond the seas; thereupon the Hui, Mo, Wa, and Han, from ten thousand li away, came to court with offerings; therefore after the Zhanghe and Yonghe reigns, embassies flowed without cease.
proposals.after: At that time the Liaodong governor Ji Rong awed the north with his might; his reputation reached beyond the seas; thereupon the Hui, Mo, Wa, and Han, from ten thousand li away, came to court with offerings; therefore after Emperors Zhang and He, embassies flowed without cease.
proposals.reason: 章、和 are Emperors Zhang and He, not Zhanghe and Yonghe reign titles.

proposals.before: Long ago Yao posted Xi Zhong to Wuyi at Yang Valley, the place where legend places the sunrise.
proposals.after: Long ago Yao ordered Xi Zhong to reside at Yu-yi, called Yang Valley, the place where the sun is said to rise.
proposals.reason: 命宅 means an order to dwell; 嵎夷 is the place Yu-yi, identified with Yang Valley, not a separate posting 'to Wuyi at' another site.

proposals.before: Once King Mu had fine steppe horses, he sent Zaofu at the reins to alert Chu and ordered a strike on Xu—the ride took a single day.
proposals.after: After King Mu obtained teams of Ji and Lu steeds, he had Zaofu drive to inform Chu and ordered an attack on Xu, arriving in a single day.
proposals.reason: 骥騄 names swift-horse teams, not generic steppe horses.

proposals.before: The king considered him divine and then listened to the mother to raise him; his name was Dongming.
proposals.after: The king considered him divine and then allowed the mother to raise him; his name was Dongming.
proposals.reason: 聽/听 here means to permit the mother to rear the child, not to listen to her words.

proposals.before: Dongming grew up skilled at archery; the king envied his fierceness and again wished to kill him.
proposals.after: Dongming grew up skilled at archery; the king feared his fierceness and again wished to kill him.
proposals.reason: 忌其猛 means the king was wary of Dongming martial prowess, not that he envied it.

proposals.before: Jianwu 32 brought tribute envoys; Emperor Guangwu restored the Koguryŏ king's rank.
proposals.after: In the eighth year of Jianwu, Koguryŏ sent tribute envoys; Emperor Guangwu restored its king's title.
proposals.reason: Chinese 建武八年 is Jianwu 8 (AD 32), not a regnal year numbered 32.

proposals.before: That winter more than ten thousand people led by the chief Dai Sheng of the Can branch tribe surrendered to Han authorities at Lelang.
proposals.after: In winter of the twenty-third year, Gouli Can-branch elder Dai Sheng and others, more than ten thousand people, went to Lelang and submitted internally.
proposals.reason: Chinese 二十三年冬 dates the submission to Jianwu 23, not the winter of the preceding sentence.

proposals.before: In spring of Jianwu 49 they struck four commanderies until Ji Rong of Liaodong coaxed them back to allegiance at the frontier.
proposals.after: In spring of the twenty-fifth year, Gouli raided Youbeiping, Yuyang, Shanggu, and Taiyuan, until Liaodong governor Ji Rong summoned them with grace and trust; all again submitted at the barrier passes.
proposals.reason: Chinese 二十五年春 is Jianwu 25 (AD 49), not Jianwu year 49.

proposals.before: In spring of Yuanxing 1 (105 CE) they swept into Liaodong and ravaged six counties until Prefect Geng Kui routed them and killed their leader.
proposals.after: In spring of Emperor He's Yuanxing first year (AD 105) they again entered Liaodong, raided and plundered six counties; prefect Geng Kui defeated them and beheaded their chieftain.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 和帝 and 復, and softens 斬其渠帥.

proposals.before: Yongchu 5 (111) brought tribute envoys from Gong asking to be placed under Xuantu command.
proposals.after: In Emperor An's Yongchu fifth year (AD 111), Gong dispatched envoys with tribute, requesting attachment to Xuantu.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 安帝 as the reigning emperor; the idiomatic English drops him.

proposals.before: Closing Chen Zhong's memorial, Emperor An approved.
proposals.after: Emperor An followed it.
proposals.reason: The Chinese is only 安帝从之; the literal line invents a memorial-closing frame not present in the source sentence.

proposals.before: Between Emperors Zhi and Huan they struck Xi'anping in Liaodong, murdered the Daifang prefect, and carried off the Lelang governor's family.
proposals.after: Between Emperors Zhi and Huan they struck Xi'anping in Liaodong, murdered the Daifang magistrate, and carried off the Lelang governor's wife and children.
proposals.reason: 帶方令 is a county magistrate (ling), not a prefect; 妻子 is specifically wife and children.

proposals.before: Shiyuan 5 (86 BCE) abolished Lintun and Zhenfan and merged them into Lelang and Xuantu.
proposals.after: Shiyuan 5 (82 BCE) abolished Lintun and Zhenfan and merged them into Lelang and Xuantu.
proposals.reason: 始元元年 is 86 BCE; 始元五年 is Emperor Zhao Shiyuan year 5, which is 82 BCE, not 86.

proposals.before: Byeonjin lies south of Jinhan with another dozen states fronting Japan.
proposals.after: Byeonjin lies south of Jinhan with another dozen states fronting Wa.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 倭, already rendered Wa elsewhere; Japan is anachronistic.

proposals.before: Near Japan to the south some practice tattooing.
proposals.after: Near Wa to the south some practice tattooing.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 倭; Japan is anachronistic relative to the source.

proposals.before: Jianwu 44 brought envoys such as Su Ma-di of the Liansi Han to Lelang with gifts.
proposals.after: In the twentieth year of Jianwu (AD 44), Han people such as Su Ma-di of Liansi went to Lelang with tribute.
proposals.reason: 建武二十年 is Jianwu year 20 (AD 44), not a reign label Jianwu 44; 韓人廉斯人 marks a Liansi man among the Han, not a polity named Liansi Han.

proposals.before: From Lelang's frontier to Wa is twelve thousand li; Kuyegan on Wa's northwest lies seven thousand li beyond.
proposals.after: From the Lelang commandery frontier to their country is twelve thousand li, and from their northwest border to Kuyegan is more than seven thousand li.
proposals.reason: The clause 去其西北界拘邪韓國七千餘里 measures distance from Wa's own northwest border to Kuyegan, not a further 7,000 li beyond Lelang.

proposals.before: Under Emperors Huan and Ling Japan fell into war without a king for years.
proposals.after: Under Emperors Huan and Ling, the state of Wa fell into great disorder and mutual attacks, remaining without a ruler for years.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English fuses Emperor Ling with Japan ('Ling Japan') and drops 更相攻伐 and 倭國 as a polity name.

proposals.before: A shaman-queen named Himiko, unmarried in age, bewitched the people into making her ruler.
proposals.after: There was a woman named Himiko, advanced in years and unmarried, who served the way of ghosts and spirits; able to bewitch the crowd with sorcery, they together established her as ruler.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line invents 'shaman-queen' as a fused title, renders 年長不嫁 unnaturally as 'unmarried in age', and omits 事鬼神道.

proposals.before: Four thousand li south stands Zhuru, whose people stand three or four feet tall.
proposals.after: More than four thousand li south of the queen's state is Zhuru, whose people are three or four chi tall.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits the origin 自女王國 and renders 尺 as English feet.

proposals.before: Legend makes Xu Fu's failed quest for Penglai end on these isles, where his thousands of colonists multiplied into myriads.
proposals.after: Tradition says Qin Shi Huang sent the fangshi Xu Fu with several thousand boys and girls to sea in search of the Penglai immortals; failing, Xu Fu feared execution, dared not return, and settled on this island, where successive generations came to number tens of thousands of households.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits 秦始皇, 方士, 童男女, 畏誅不敢還, and 世世相承, collapsing a full legend into a vague summary.

proposals.before: That is the essence of how sages frame law—sparse statutes grounded in trust."
proposals.after: If, like Jizi, one trims the statutes and relies on good faith, one touches the very root from which the sages fashioned law!"
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the explicit comparison to Jizi (若箕子) and the closing force of the essay's quoted judgment.

decisions.reason: 章、和 matches the emperor-pair pattern of 桓、靈 in the next sentences, not the era names Zhanghe or Yonghe; 韓 is the Han peoples of this treatise, not a general 'Korea'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 濊、貊、倭、韓，萬里朝獻，故章、和已後

decisions.reason: The literal line wrongly treats 章、和 as reign titles Zhanghe and Yonghe; they are Emperors Zhang and He, after whose time 使聘流通.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 故章、和已後，使聘流通

decisions.reason: 命…宅 is an order to dwell at 嵎夷, which the text names 旸谷; the original turns that identification into a posting 'to Wuyi at' a second site.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔堯命羲仲宅嵎夷，曰旸谷

decisions.reason: 骥騄之乘 are named swift-horse teams obtained later (後得), not generic steppe horses introduced by 'once'.

decisions.reason: 听母收養 is permission for the mother to rear the child, not listening to her advice; the idiomatic line already has this sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃听母收養

decisions.reason: 忌其猛 is wary fear of Dongming's fierceness, which motivates 復欲殺之; 'envied' invents jealousy.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王忌其猛，復欲殺之

decisions.reason: 'That winter' wrongly ties 二十三年冬 to Jianwu 8; the proposed wording is accurate but needs Gouli's as a possessive so Can-branch elder is grammatical.

decisions.after: In spring of Yuanxing 1 (AD 105) under Emperor He they again swept into Liaodong and ravaged six counties until Prefect Geng Kui routed them and beheaded their chieftain.
decisions.reason: The original omits 和帝 and 復 and weakens 斬其渠帥 to 'killed'; the proposal is right on substance but needlessly replaces already accurate idiomatic verbs.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 和帝元兴元年春，復入遼東，寇略六縣，太守耿夔擊破之，斬其渠帥

decisions.reason: Yongchu 5 (111) already dates Gong's tribute and Xuantu request; naming 安帝 is recoverable from that unique era and the rewrite is stylistic.

decisions.reason: 安帝从之 only says Emperor An followed the advice; 'Closing Chen Zhong's memorial' is not in this sentence.

decisions.reason: 帶方令 is a county magistrate, not a prefect; 妻子 is the governor's wife and children, not a vague 'family'.

decisions.reason: 昭帝始元五年 is Shiyuan 5 of Emperor Zhao, 82 BCE; 86 BCE is Shiyuan 1.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建武二十年，韓人廉斯人苏馬諟等

decisions.after: From the Lelang commandery frontier to their country is twelve thousand li, and to Kuyegan, their northwest border, more than seven thousand li.
decisions.reason: Both versions misread 去其西北界拘邪韓國: the Lelang frontier is 12,000 li from Wa and 7,000-odd li from Kuyegan, which is Wa's northwest bound, not a further leg from that bound.
